confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from a few web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites (Mylifeelsewhere, Traveltables, Livingcost, Nomad Ranker, Expatistan). These sources differ in date (2023 to 2026) and method, and they disagree on some items. Cappuccino was about $1.8–2.2 on most of them. Restaurant draught beer was about $4.8–5.8 on most. An inexpensive meal was about $8.5–12.3, and a mid-range dinner for two about $42–52. I found no cocktail prices, so the cocktail is set at roughly twice the restaurant beer price, in line with typical Italian bar pricing. The wine glass is also an estimate, based on a bar or restaurant glass of house wine and local bottle prices. The RBA rate is the latest figure I found, from a search result snippet that cited the RBA overview page, not from reading the page directly. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from live listings. They assume July 2026 peak-season demand in Palermo and are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Palermo is a lower-cost southern Italian city. Search results put restaurant prices about 14% below the Italian average and well below Rome. Its prices resemble those of Naples and Catania, with tourist-area premiums in the historic centre. Accommodation is a holistic estimate, scaled up for July peak season.
